A barre chord uses the index finger laid flat across all six strings as a movable nut, with the other fingers forming an open chord shape above it. The E shape and the A shape let you play any major or minor chord by sliding along the neck. The index finger should roll slightly onto its bony side, and the pressure comes from pulling back with the arm rather than squeezing with the thumb. Buzzing is normal for weeks. They build on [[Guitar chords for beginners]].
